Five months after a ceasefire was supposedly announced, we are witnessing the ongoing devastation of the Palestinian people—a profound moral failure rooted in systemic violence, institutional complicity, and the relentless oppression of a vulnerable population. Airstrikes and military aggression continue to take civilian lives while the humanitarian crisis is left to fester. This is nothing less than the structural erasure of a community, designed to strip a people of their history, dignity, and basic human rights. 

As 56-year-old Ahmed Baroud, a father of five currently displaced in Deir al-Balah, powerfully pointed out: “Drones never stop buzzing overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily and naval boats fire towards fishermen.” 

This brutality is reshaping existence into a nightmare entirely disconnected from any prewar reality. The international institutions that refuse to enforce true justice and dismantle these systems of oppression must be held fully accountable for their inaction in the face of such profound injustice.
